questions.question: Why is legal enforceability of rules important in a society?

options.text: It provides assurance that others will follow the rules.
It gives power to the police only.
So people can break them without fear

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides assurance that others will follow the rules.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Legal enforceability ensures that individuals adhere to societal rules and regulations, fostering a harmonious and orderly environment.
 
• It creates a system of accountability, deterring people from violating laws due to potential penalties.
 
• A legally enforced framework maintains fairness and equality by applying rules uniformly to all members of society.
 
• It provides a sense of security, as individuals trust that disputes or violations will be resolved through an impartial legal process.
 
• By ensuring compliance, legal enforceability aids in preventing anarchy and upholding social order and justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal enforceability:** Refers to the formal application of laws by authorities to ensure compliance and address violations.
 
• **Rule of law:** A principle under which all individuals, institutions, and entities are accountable to laws that are fairly applied and enforced.
 
• **Justice system:** Plays a crucial role in enforcing legal rules, resolving disputes, and penalizing unlawful actions to maintain social harmony.
 
• **Social contract theory:** Suggests that individuals consent to follow rules and laws in exchange for protection and benefits provided by the society and state.
 
• **Consequences of lawlessness:** Lack of legal enforceability can lead to chaos, increased crime rates, and the breakdown of societal structures.

questions.question: Which body acts as the apex at the district level in Panchayati Raj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zilla Parishad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Zilla Parishad** is the apex body at the district level in the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in India.
 
• It functions as the governing and administrative authority for rural development and local self-governance at the district level.
 
• The Zilla Parishad supervises and coordinates the activities of the Panchayat Samiti and Gram Panchayat under its jurisdiction.
 
• The members of the Zilla Parishad are elected representatives from various constituencies within the district.
 
• It is headed by the President, who is elected from among its members, with the District Collector serving as the administrative link between the Zilla Parishad and the state government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayati Raj System:**

 
 
• It is a decentralized form of governance introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992.
 
• It consists of a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zilla Parishad (district level).
 
• This system empowers local self-governance and promotes participatory democracy.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Zilla Parishad:**
 
 
• Formulates and implements development plans for the district, focusing on areas such as health, education, and agriculture.
 
• Coordinates the activities of various departments and monitors the execution of government programs.
 
• Allocates funds to Panchayat Samitis and oversees their utilization.
 
 
 
• **Composition of Zilla Parishad:**
 
 
• It consists of elected members, representatives of Panchayat Samitis, and members of the Legislative Assembly and Parliament from the district.
 
• Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women as per constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Key Legislations:**
 
 
• The Panchayati Raj System operates under the provisions of the **73rd Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is governed by state-specific Panchayati Raj Acts, which outline the roles, responsibilities, and powers of the Zilla Parishad.

questions.question: Which river in Jammu and Kashmir has the world’s highest railway bridge built over it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chenab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir is home to the world's highest railway bridge, known as the **Chenab Bridge**.
 
• The Chenab Bridge is part of the **Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project** undertaken by the Indian Railways.
 
• It stands at a height of **359 meters (1,178 feet)** above the riverbed, making it taller than the Eiffel Tower.
 
• The bridge spans **1,315 meters** and is designed to withstand wind speeds up to 266 km/h and earthquakes of high intensity.
 
• Construction of the Chenab Bridge was completed in **2022**, marking a significant engineering achievement in challenging terrain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chenab River:** It originates from the Baralacha Pass in Himachal Pradesh and flows through Jammu and Kashmir before entering Pakistan.
 
• **USBRL Project:** This ambitious rail link aims to connect the Kashmir Valley with the rest of India, enhancing connectivity and boosting regional development.
 
• **Engineering Challenges:** The construction of the Chenab Bridge involved overcoming steep gorges, high-altitude conditions, and seismic challenges.
 
• **Steel Arch Design:** The bridge has a steel arch design, making it resilient against geological and climatic challenges in the Himalayan region.
 
• **Strategic Importance:** The bridge plays a crucial role in improving transportation and economic integration in Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.question: Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy was added by the Forty-fourth Amendment Act, 1978?

options.text: Protection and improvement of the environment and wildlife
Provision for free legal aid to the poor
Participation of workers in industrial management
Reduction of inequalities in income and status among individuals and groups

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduction of inequalities in income and status among individuals and groups**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Change: It added Article 38(2) to the Constitution.
 
• The Goal: It tells the government to reduce the gap between the rich and the poor.
 
• Beyond Money: It’s not just about income; the government must also work to give everyone equal status, better facilities, and fair opportunities.
 
• It focuses on helping both individuals and groups (like people in different jobs or different regions).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):** The DPSPs are guidelines for the state to frame policies and laws aimed at establishing social and economic democracy in the country.
 
• **44th Amendment Act, 1978:** In addition to adding Article 38(2), this amendment also made significant changes, such as restoring the right to property as a legal right rather than a fundamental right.
 
• **Article 39:** It provides for the principles of policy that aim to ensure adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, and protection against economic exploitation.
 
• **Legal Aid System in India:** The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) was set up under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, to provide free legal aid to marginalized sections of society.
 
• **Fundamental Rights vs Directive Principles:** While Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the courts, DPSPs are non-justiciable but act as guiding principles for governance.

questions.question: Identify the language which is primarily spoken in the state of Mizoram in India from the options below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mizo** is the primary language spoken in Mizoram, a state in northeastern India.
 
• The Mizo language is a part of the Tibeto-Burman language family, widely spoken by the Mizos.
 
• Mizo is the official language of Mizoram and is used in government, education, and communication.
 
• The language is also known as Lushai or Duhlian, although "Mizo" is the preferred term.
 
• Mizo is written using the Roman script, which was introduced by Christian missionaries during the colonial period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mizoram:** Mizoram is one of the northeastern states of India, with Aizawl as its capital.
 
• **Mizo Culture:** The Mizo people have a rich cultural heritage with traditional dances like Cheraw and music playing a significant role.
 
• **Other Languages:** While Mizo is predominant, other languages such as Lai, Mara, and Chakma are also spoken in Mizoram.
 
• **Christian Missionaries:** Missionaries were instrumental in the spread of Christianity in Mizoram and contributed to the development of the Mizo script.
 
• **Mizo Literature:** Mizo literature primarily consists of folk songs, proverbs, and modern writings that reflect the culture and traditions of the Mizo people.

questions.question: How does the use of renewable energy contribute to sustainable development?

options.text: It provides unlimited profits to energy companies.
It increases dependency on fossil fuels.
It reduces environmental pollution and conserves resources

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It reduces environmental pollution and conserves resources**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power, produce little to no greenhouse gas emissions, helping mitigate climate change.
 
• Unlike fossil fuels, renewable energy sources do not deplete finite natural resources, ensuring long-term availability.
 
• By reducing air and water pollution, renewable energy contributes to better public health and reduced healthcare costs.
 
• Renewable energy supports energy security by reducing dependency on imported fuels and diversifying energy sources.
 
• It promotes economic development by creating jobs in the renewable energy sector and fostering innovation in green technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Renewable Energy:** Energy derived from natural sources that are replenished constantly, such as sunlight, wind, and water.
 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emissions:** Gases like carbon dioxide and methane that trap heat in the atmosphere, leading to global warming.
 
• **Energy Security:** The ability of a nation to ensure reliable and affordable energy supply for its population and economy.
 
• **Sustainable Development:** Development that meets current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
 
• **Environmental Pollution:** The contamination of air, water, and soil due to harmful substances, which can be reduced by adopting clean energy solutions.

questions.question: Which colonial policy is often blamed for the decline of India's traditional handicraft industries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**De-industrialisation policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The British colonial policy of **de-industrialisation** led to the systematic decline of India's traditional handicraft industries.
 
• Under British rule, India was transformed into an exporter of raw materials and an importer of British manufactured goods, disrupting indigenous industries.
 
• Heavy taxation and the influx of cheap machine-made British goods destroyed the market for handmade Indian products like textiles and handicrafts.
 
• The decline of handicraft industries led to widespread unemployment among artisans and craftsmen, adversely impacting local economies.
 
• The de-industrialisation policy was a key factor in the economic stagnation of India during the colonial period, contributing to poverty and dependency on agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Revolution and De-industrialisation:** The Industrial Revolution in Britain enabled mass production of goods, replacing handmade Indian products in international markets.
 
• **Drain of Wealth Theory:** Economic historian Dadabhai Naoroji highlighted how the British drained India's wealth through unfair trade practices and exploitation.
 
• **Impact on Indian Textile Industry:** India’s flourishing textile industry was heavily impacted as British goods flooded the markets, forcing many weavers to abandon their traditional crafts.
 
• **Shift to Agriculture:** With the collapse of handicrafts, a significant portion of the population shifted to agriculture, increasing dependency and creating economic imbalances.
 
• **Rise of Famines:** The economic policies led to reduced income and widespread poverty, contributing to frequent famines during British rule in India.

questions.question: Which is the deadliest species of Plasmodium that causes malaria in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmodium falciparum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasmodium falciparum** is the deadliest species of Plasmodium responsible for malaria in humans.
 
• It causes the most severe form of malaria, known as **malignant malaria**, which can lead to cerebral malaria and organ failure.
 
• This species is responsible for the majority of malaria-related deaths globally, especially in sub-Saharan Africa.
 
• Plasmodium falciparum has a high reproduction rate in red blood cells, leading to severe anemia and complications.
 
• The parasite has developed resistance to some antimalarial drugs, making treatment and control challenging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium species:** There are five species of Plasmodium known to infect humans: P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale, and P. knowlesi.
 
• **Life cycle of Plasmodium:** The parasite has a complex life cycle involving two hosts: the Anopheles mosquito (vector) and humans.
 
• **Cerebral malaria:** A severe form of malaria caused by P. falciparum, leading to neurological complications such as seizures, coma, and even death.
 
• **Drug resistance:** P. falciparum has shown resistance to multiple antimalarial drugs, including chloroquine, making treatment more difficult.
 
• **Global impact:** Malaria caused by P. falciparum is a major public health issue, with the World Health Organization (WHO) estimating over 600,000 deaths annually, mostly among children under five years of age in Africa.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between the Cabinet and the Council of Ministers?

options.text: The Cabinet is not part of the executive, but the Council is part of the executive
The Cabinet is larger and includes all ministers, while the Council is a smaller group
The Cabinet includes senior ministers, while the Council includes all categories of ministers
The Council of Ministers does not include the Prime Minister

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Cabinet includes senior ministers, while the Council includes all categories of ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cabinet is a smaller body within the Council of Ministers, composed of senior ministers holding important portfolios such as Finance, Defence, and Home Affairs.
 
• The Council of Ministers consists of three categories: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
 
• The Cabinet is the decision-making body responsible for major policies and key issues, while the Council of Ministers assists in broader governmental functions.
 
• The Prime Minister is part of both the Cabinet and the Council of Ministers, serving as the head of the government.
 
• The Cabinet exercises executive authority and is collectively responsible to the Parliament, particularly the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cabinet Ministers:** These are senior members of the Council of Ministers who head important ministries like Finance, Defence, Home, External Affairs, etc.
 
• **Ministers of State:** These are junior ministers who either work independently or assist Cabinet Ministers in their duties.
 
• **Deputy Ministers:** They assist both Cabinet Ministers and Ministers of State in their specific responsibilities.
 
• ** The Council of Ministers, including the Cabinet, is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha as per Article 75 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Prime Minister's Role:** The Prime Minister leads the Cabinet and the Council of Ministers, acts as the chief advisor to the President, and coordinates the functioning of all ministries.

questions.question: The Immigration and Foreigners Bill 2025, repeals which of the following Acts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Immigration and Foreigners Bill 2025 aims to modernize and consolidate laws related to immigration and foreigners in India.
 
• The bill seeks to repeal the **Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920**, which governs the entry of foreigners into India through passports and visas.
 
• This Act was enacted during the colonial era and is considered outdated in addressing modern-day immigration challenges.
 
• The new bill emphasizes streamlining immigration processes and addressing issues such as illegal immigration and national security concerns.
 
• The proposed legislation introduces enhanced measures for monitoring, regulating, and facilitating immigration in alignment with current global standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920:**

 
 
• It was implemented during British rule in India to regulate the entry of foreigners.
 
• Required individuals entering India to hold valid passports or travel documents.
 
• Primarily focused on controlling immigration during colonial times.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010:**
 
 
• Regulates the acceptance and utilization of foreign contributions by individuals, associations, and companies.
 
• Aims to prevent misuse of foreign funds for activities detrimental to national interests.
 
 
 
• **Emigration Act, 1983:**
 
 
• Deals with the regulation of emigration of Indian citizens for employment abroad.
 
• Provides safeguards to protect Indian workers from exploitation overseas.
 
 
 
• **Immigration (Carriers Liability) Amendment Act, 2005:**
 
 
• Imposes obligations on carriers to ensure passengers have valid travel documents before entering India.
 
• Part of efforts to control illegal immigration into the country.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of primary memory in a computer?

options.text: It is slower than secondary memory.
It is used to back up files externally.
It holds data temporarily for quick access during processing.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It holds data temporarily for quick access during processing.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Primary memory is a volatile form of memory, meaning it stores data temporarily and loses data when the power is turned off.
 
• It facilitates quick access to data, enabling faster execution of processes by the CPU during computation.
 
• Examples of primary memory include RAM (Random Access Memory) and cache memory, which provide high-speed data retrieval.
 
• The main function of primary memory is to store data and instructions that are actively being used by the CPU.
 
• Primary memory is much faster but has limited storage capacity compared to secondary memory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Memory:** Also called main memory, it includes RAM and ROM. RAM is volatile, while ROM is non-volatile and stores essential system instructions.
 
• **Secondary Memory:** Non-volatile storage used for long-term data storage, such as hard drives, SSDs, and external storage devices.
 
• **Cache Memory:** A smaller, faster type of volatile memory located close to the CPU, it stores frequently used data for quick access.
 
• **Volatile vs. Non-Volatile Memory:** Volatile memory (e.g., RAM) requires power to maintain data, whereas non-volatile memory (e.g., ROM, SSD) retains data even when powered off.
 
• **Memory Hierarchy:** Primary memory is at the top of the memory hierarchy due to its speed, followed by secondary and tertiary storage options.

questions.question: What is the area around the equator called where the trade winds from both hemispheres converge?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a region near the equator where trade winds from the northern and southern hemispheres converge.
 
• This convergence causes warm, moist air to rise, leading to frequent thunderstorms and heavy precipitation.
 
• The ITCZ shifts north and south of the equator throughout the year due to the Earth's axial tilt and orbit around the Sun.
 
• It is often referred to as the "doldrums" because of the calm winds and low-pressure conditions that prevail in this region.
 
• The ITCZ plays a critical role in global weather patterns and is a major factor in the formation of tropical cyclones and monsoon systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade Winds:** These are steady winds that blow from the east towards the equator, originating from the high-pressure regions in both hemispheres.
 
• **Polar Front:** This is the boundary between the cold polar air masses and the warmer air masses of the mid-latitudes, unrelated to the ITCZ.
 
• **Horse Latitudes:** These are regions of high pressure and calm winds located at about 30°N and 30°S latitudes, distinct from the ITCZ.
 
• **Monsoons:** The shifting of the ITCZ plays a significant role in the development of monsoon systems, especially in regions like South Asia and West Africa.
 
• **Climatic Impact:** The ITCZ contributes to the tropical climate and is responsible for the wet and dry seasons in equatorial regions.

questions.question: Which neighbouring country of India is an island nation in the Indian Ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maldives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• It consists of approximately 1,192 coral islands grouped in 26 atolls, making it one of the most geographically dispersed countries in the world.
 
• Malé is the capital city of the Maldives and is one of the smallest capitals in the world.
 
• The Maldives is renowned for its tourism industry, featuring luxury resorts and pristine beaches, attracting millions of visitors annually.
 
• It is also the lowest-lying country globally, with an average elevation of just 1.5 meters above sea level, making it highly vulnerable to climate change and rising sea levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Location:** The Maldives lies strategically in the Indian Ocean, forming an important maritime route between the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
 
• **Economy:** Tourism is the largest contributor to the Maldivian economy, with fisheries and agriculture playing secondary roles.
 
• **Historical Significance:** The Maldives has a rich cultural heritage influenced by South Asian, Arab, and African cultures due to its location along ancient trade routes.
 
• **Political Structure:** The Maldives is a presidential republic, and its current constitution was adopted in 2008.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** The Maldives is actively involved in international efforts to combat climate change, as rising sea levels threaten its existence.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an operating system commonly used on laptops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows 11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Windows 11** is the latest operating system developed by Microsoft, specifically designed to optimize performance and user experience on laptops and PCs.
 
• It was officially released on **October 5, 2021**, as the successor to Windows 10.
 
• The operating system features a redesigned user interface, including a centered Start menu, updated taskbar, and new window management tools like Snap Layouts.
 
• Windows 11 supports enhanced security features such as **Secure Boot, TPM 2.0, and Windows Hello** for biometric authentication.
 
• It is compatible with most modern laptops and desktops, provided they meet specific hardware requirements, such as a minimum of 4GB RAM and 64GB storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operating System (OS):**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution defines the money bill?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 110**__.

__
 
• **Article 110** of the Indian Constitution defines what constitutes a Money Bill.
 
• A Money Bill deals exclusively with matters specified in Article 110(1), such as taxation, public expenditure, and borrowing by the government.
 
• Money Bills can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha** and require the recommendation of the President of India before introduction.
 
• The Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha can accept or reject.
 
• Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not.

• **Money Bill:** A type of financial legislation that deals solely with financial matters specified in Article 110, such as imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes.
 
• **Difference from Financial Bill:** A Financial Bill can include provisions related to money matters but also contains clauses beyond the scope of Article 110. It can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
 
• **Procedure for Money Bill:** After passing the Lok Sabha, the Money Bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha, which must return it within 14 days. If not returned, it is deemed to be passed.
 
• **Examples of Money Bills:** Appropriation Bill and Finance Bill are examples of Money Bills in India.
 
• **Role of President:** The President's recommendation is mandatory for introducing a Money Bill in the Lok Sabha, as per Article 110.

• They aimed to liberalize the Indian economy by reducing tariffs, deregulating markets, and opening up the economy to foreign investments.
 
• The policy marked a significant departure from the License Raj system, allowing industries to grow with fewer restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of License Raj on Industry:**
 
 
• Discouraged entrepreneurship and innovation due to excessive bureaucratic control.
 
• Led to inefficiencies and delays in industrial projects.
 
• Encouraged corruption as businesses often had to bribe officials to obtain licenses.
 
 
 
• **Post-1991 Industrial Growth:**

• Industries experienced greater autonomy and growth due to the reduction of restrictive regulations.

questions.question: What is the phenomenon called when a wire passes through a block of ice without splitting it and the water refreezes after the wire passes?

• **Regelation** is the phenomenon where ice melts under pressure and refreezes when the pressure is removed.
 
• When a wire passes through a block of ice, the pressure at the contact point causes the ice to melt momentarily into water.
 
• The water formed due to melting refreezes after the wire passes, demonstrating the process of regelation.
 
• This occurs because the melting point of ice decreases when pressure increases, allowing the ice to melt locally without breaking.
 
• Regelation is a property unique to substances like ice, which expand upon freezing, unlike most materials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fusion:** It is the process of changing a solid into a liquid at its melting point by absorbing heat.
 
• **Condensation:** This refers to the transformation of water vapor into liquid water, typically due to cooling.
 
• **Sublimation:** It is the direct transition of a substance from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state.
 
• The concept of regelation is used in applications such as ice skating, where pressure from the blade momentarily melts the ice, reducing friction.
 
• Regelation is possible because ice has a negative slope in its pressure-temperature phase diagram, meaning increased pressure lowers its melting point.

questions.question: If the 6-digit number N29M11 is divisible by 11, then which of the options below can give a possible correct relation between M and N?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For divisibility by 11, the difference of the sums of alternate digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Sum of odd position digits = N + 9 + 1 = N + 10

Sum of even position digits = 2 + M + 1 = M + 3

Difference = (N + 10) − (M + 3) = N − M + 7

Equating to 0 for a valid single-digit relation: N − M + 7 = 0 ⇒ M − N = 7.

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The 6-digit number is N29M11, and it is perfectly divisible by 11.

**Concept Used:**

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The given number = N29M11

⇒ Sum of digits at odd places (from left to right) = N + 9 + 1 = N + 10

⇒ Sum of digits at even places (from left to right) = 2 + M + 1 = M + 3

⇒ Difference = (Sum of odd places) − (Sum of even places)

⇒ Difference = (N + 10) − (M + 3)

⇒ Difference = N − M + 7

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 11, this difference must be equal to 0, 11, or a multiple of 11.

⇒ Case 1: Equating difference to 0

⇒ N − M + 7 = 0

⇒ M − N = 7

⇒ Case 2: Equating difference to 11

⇒ N − M + 7 = 11

⇒ N − M = 4

⇒ Since M and N are single digits, both relations are mathematically possible, but only M − N = 7 is present among the given choices.

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3 and 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Combined Divisibility Rule of 7, 11, and 13

If the difference between the number formed by the last three digits and the number formed by the remaining leading digits is divisible by 7, 11, or 13, then the original number is divisible by 7, 11, or 13 respectively.
</p

questions.question: By availing two successive discounts of 20% and 10%, a customer got a discount of ₹23,800. Determine the marked price of the item.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equivalent discount % for successive discounts of 20% and 10% = 20 + 10 − (20 × 10) ÷ 100 = 28%.

Given that 28% of the Marked Price = ₹23,800.

⇒ MP = (23,800 ÷ 28) × 100 = 850 × 100 = ₹85,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹85,000.**

**Given:**

Successive discounts = 20% and 10%

Total discount obtained = ₹23,800

**Formula Used:**

Effective Discount % = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100

Discount = Marked Price (MP) − Selling Price (SP)

⇒ SP after further 10% discount = 80x − 10% of 80x = 72x

**Given:**

**Method Used:**

Primality test: A number N is prime if it is not divisible by any prime number ≤ √N.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total numbers to check: 393, 394, 395, 396, 397, 398, 399, 400, 401

⇒ Even numbers greater than 2 are not prime. Discard 394, 396, 398, 400.

⇒ Numbers ending in 5 are not prime. Discard 395.

⇒ Numbers whose digit sum is a multiple of 3 are not prime. Discard 393 (3 + 9 + 3 = 15) and 399 (3 + 9 + 9 = 21).

⇒ Only 397 and 401 remain as potential prime numbers.

⇒ For 397: √397 ≈ 19.9. Prime numbers ≤ 19 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. 397 is not divisible by any of them. ∴ 397 is a prime number.

⇒ For 401: √401 ≈ 20.02. Prime numbers ≤ 19 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. 401 is not divisible by any of them. ∴ 401 is a prime number.

⇒ Total prime numbers between 393 and 401 = 2 (which are 397 and 401).

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that cannot be formed by multiplying two smaller natural numbers. It has exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself.

Primality Test

To check if a number 'N' is prime, find its approximate square root (√N). If 'N' is not divisible by any prime number less than or equal to √N, then 'N' is a prime number.

Divisibility Rules

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is 0 or 5. A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

questions.question: The sum of the squares of two consecutive even natural numbers is 1460. The sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the average of the two consecutive even numbers be a. The numbers will be (a − 1) and (a + 1).

Sum of their squares = (a − 1)² + (a + 1)² = 2(a² + 1)

⇒ 2(a² + 1) = 1460 ⇒ a² + 1 = 730 ⇒ a² = 729 ⇒ a = 27

The numbers are 26 and 28. Their sum is 26 + 28 = 54.

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The sum of the squares of two consecutive even natural numbers is 1460.

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculation:**

Let the two consecutive even natural numbers be x and (x + 2).

According to the given condition:

⇒ x² + (x + 2)² = 1460

⇒ x² + x² + 4x + 4 = 1460

⇒ 2x² + 4x + 4 = 1460

⇒ 2x² + 4x − 1456 = 0

Dividing the entire equation by 2:

⇒ x² + 2x − 728 = 0

Factorising the quadratic equation:

⇒ x² + 28x − 26x − 728 = 0

⇒ x(x + 28) − 26(x + 28) = 0

⇒ (x − 26)(x + 28) = 0

⇒ x = 26 or x = −28

Since the numbers are natural numbers, x must be positive. Therefore, x = 26.

⇒ The second consecutive even number = x + 2 = 26 + 2 = 28.

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 26 + 28 = 54.

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Even and Odd Numbers

Consecutive even integers are always represented as 2n, 2n+2, 2n+4, etc. Consecutive odd integers are represented as 2n+1, 2n+3, 2n+5, etc.

Quadratic Formula

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the exact roots can be found using the formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.

Sum and Product of Roots

For the general quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of the roots is equal to −b/a and the product of the roots is equal to c/a.
